content:
matt: Heads up — after the v2.18.3 rollout I'm seeing 4 longctx OOMs on prod-us-west-2 within the last hour. Happening on GPU pool A, all with high seqlen traffic. Logs attached below.

matt: ```
runtime: oom: alloc failed after 1.2GB used
context: seq_len=4096, kv_cache_slots=32768
stack: runtime/kv_cache.cpp:421 evict_window_rotate
```

anya: which commit landed in that rollout? any config flips?

matt: commit `a8bc12f` — changed slab rotation heuristic + defaulted `batching.max_seq_group` to 8 (was 4). No explicit revert yet.

dmitri: started a quick perf recording on one of the failed boxes. Early signal: slab churn up ~3x, many short-lived allocations, and mmap calls spike. Looks like rotation is forcing frequent slab migrations. profile snippet: `kv_slab_free_rate +2.9x, mmap_count +180%`.

carla: hmm. we also pushed the kernel-selection change that prefers `fast-kernel-v3` for seq_len>1024. That kernel has different allocation alignment that interacts with our slab strata. Could be causing fragmentation when combined with larger batch groups.

ryan: CI alerted earlier: `perf/seqlen-stress` failing on the perf-job (seqlen=4096) around the same merge set. Failed test is `kv_cache_stability_test` — job link: https://ci.internal/perf/7821

ci-bot: [deploybot] Rolling deploy triggered: v2.18.3 -> rolling strategy: gradual-canary (20%) -> current: 45% -> paused due to errors.

anya: can someone run `rwdctl kv stats --pool A --dump` on a canary box and paste output? we need slab occupancy, fragment count, and eviction_windows.

matt: pasted minimal dump: `slots_total=32768 slots_used=31400 slab_frag=0.37 eviction_windows=7 rotation_count=18964` — slab_frag ratio higher than baseline (0.12).

dmitri: bisect plan: I'll run a two-way bisect between `a8bc12f` and the parent that changed kernel selection `f3d9e21`. Script: `git bisect start; git bisect bad a8bc12f; git bisect good f3d9e21~1; for each commit run quick-stress --seqlen 4096 --duration 60s`. Should find culprit in ~6 runs.

carla: also test reverting only the slab-rotation flag locally (no kernel change) to isolate. If revert fixes fragmentation, then kernel selection and batching interaction is likely compounding.

ryan: marking this as rollout-blocker. Opening an emergency revert PR for the slab rotation heuristic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4897 (WIP).

ci-bot: [ci] perf/seqlen-stress queued for branch revert-4897, run id 7832.

anya: matt, can you run a quick canary rollback to 2.18.2 on the two most-impacted hosts? we should stop new failures while bisect runs.

matt: doing now. rolling back 2 hosts to 2.18.2 -> `ok` on host-12, host-19. Observing reduced memory pressure after ~30s.

dmitri: bisect found the regression: commit `a8bc12f` (slab rotation heuristic) + interaction with `fast-kernel-v3` yields high fragmentation for long sequences when batching group >4. Repro steps attached.

carla: thanks. PR 4897 ready to merge to revert rotation heuristic. Please run perf/seqlen-stress on staging with `fast-kernel-v3` + revert to confirm.

ryan: once confirmed we'll re-run the rollout with smaller `batching.max_seq_group=4` as an extra safety net. Also create an automated canary check that watches slab_frag >0.2 and auto-pauses rollout.

matt: noted. created alert `kv_slab_frag_high` -> pager on severity P1.

anya: good catch everyone. follow-ups: (1) revert PR -> merge, (2) add regression test for slab_frag thresholds to perf CI, (3) audit kernel-selection alignment assumptions.

carla: assigning tasks: dmitri -> perf test additions, matt -> rollout/alerts, ryan -> PR review + canary rule, anya -> postmortem stub. :thumbsup:

ryan: can we close this thread after PR merged and perf pass? I'll shepherd the staging run.

ci-bot: [deploybot] rollback to v2.18.2 completed for hosts host-12, host-19.

matt: PR merged and staging perf pass looks green. moving to postmortem. Great triage team. :party:
